history.dynasty: Ancient temple; exterior sabhamandap dated 1936 AD (Kaavi art)
history.summary: An ancient temple at Morjim in Pernem taluka dedicated to Goddess Shri Morjai, said to be one of seven sisters who came and settled in different parts of Goa along with their brother Shri Khetoba. The temple walls and the original mukhmandap are decorated with rare 'Kaavi' art friezes — red-and-white lime-plaster murals with geometric and floral patterns — and the exterior sabhamandap dates to 1936 AD. The principal festival is the Kalas Utsav, celebrated once every three, five, seven or nine years for nearly a month from Phalgun Shuddha Panchami. Scholars note Morjai as one of Goa's ancient village goddesses now worshipped in formalised temple settings. CSV TOWN CORRECTED: the temple is at Morjim village — Pernem is the taluka/town about 11 km away. Coordinates from two independent location listings (15.63606, 73.73994).

name: Shri Morjai Temple
town_description: Morjim is a coastal village in Pernem taluka of North Goa, known for its long sandy beach and as a nesting site for Olive Ridley sea turtles. A short distance inland from the beach, the village keeps a traditional Goan character with palm groves and paddy fields, and is home to the historic Shri Morjai temple with its rare Kaavi art friezes.
